122	of the months. The first month is Nisan, so
123	Sivan is the third month. The letter connected with
124	the number three is the letter
125	Gimel. Tamuz is the fourth of the
126	months. The letter connected with Tamuz is the letter
127	Dalet. And as we move from Sivan to Tamuz, on Shabbat
128	we bless, God willing, tomorrow in the synagogue,
129	after the Torah reading, we will bless Rosh Chodesh
130	Tamuz, which comes upon us for good, and it falls, with HaShem's help,
131	on Rosh Chodesh Tamuz, which comes upon us for good, and it falls on
132	Shabbat Kodesh, and the next day, Sunday, and the day after it. So
133	the blessing is really a kind of drawing down and giving of strength
134	from this Shabbat, and our presence now in the month of Sivan,
135	to the month of Tamuz, the coming month. That is to say, there is
136	a connection between the Gimel
137	and the Dalet. The Sages say: what is the hint in the letters?
138	Gimel, Dalet: "gomel dalim,"
139	"he bestows on the poor." Gimel is from the word gomel, which is really the act of
140	giving,
141	of the one who bestows. And so too in the letters of the Holy Tongue, everything
142	is perfectly precise. The shape of the letter Gimel in the Holy Tongue
143	is like a Vav that has a hand
144	outstretched. It is like the giver who stretches out his hand. Where does he stretch out his hand? Toward the next
145	letter,
146	the Dalet. The letter Dalet, in contrast,
147	is just as its name suggests: just as Gimel is gomel, so Dalet
148	is from the word dal, poor. The Gimel bestows on one who has nothing,
149	on the poor. And how do I know that the Dalet receives from the Gimel? Because the Dalet
150	stretches out a hand toward the Gimel. Where is the hand of the Dalet? The Dalet
151	is, after all, like
152	the Resh. But the Resh has no hand; the Resh has pride. It
153	does not want to receive from anyone. Not so the Dalet, which
154	stretches out its hand to the Gimel to receive
155	the flow. And when the flow passes from the Gimel to the Dalet, in effect
156	the power of the third month, which is the power of the Torah,
157	the light of the Torah, descends below, to the world, for this
158	world
159	is divided into four. Why is the world divided into four? The Torah is connected
160	to three. The Torah has Torah, Prophets,
161	and Writings. The Torah was given to us in the third month,
162	on the third day, through the third one, who is Moshe
163	Rabbeinu. It was given to the people of Israel, who are divided into three:
164	Kohanim, Levi'im, and Yisraelim. In the letters of the Torah there are
165	three kinds of letters: large letters,
166	medium letters, and
167	small letters. And there are many more matters of three in the Torah.
168	The whole Torah revolves around the matter of three,
169	because the matter of three is the matter of peace, of
170	strength. Shalom is also the numerical value of "chazakah," but in the context
171	of ours now, the whole Torah was given to make peace
172	in the world. On the second day there was division, and this is exactly the power of
173	the third, which brings the power of peace to make
174	peace between the dispute of the two. For how does the Torah
175	make peace? Right, how does the Torah make peace?
176	Since the Torah is the wisdom of HaShem, and one becomes one
177	with HaShem, blessed be He, when you reveal the power of
178	the Holy One, blessed be He, in every
179	situation, suddenly you notice that although
180	there can be enormous disputes between Beit Hillel
181	and Beit Shammai, not to mention that those are disputes for the sake of
182	Heaven, not to mention other disputes, still, where is there room
183	for dispute?
184	When we are speaking
185	of the opinion of the lower person, in whose opinion, since
186	it is limited, he can grasp things
187	in a very particular way, and just as their faces are not
188	alike, so their opinions are not alike. So in opinion there can
189	be a dispute, but the moment they reveal the opinion of
190	the Torah, that the Torah reveals HaShem, then of course
191	peace is made. Therefore the whole Torah is connected to the number
192	three, which is the power to make peace between the two
193	who dispute
194	with each other. But this Torah, from its power to make
195	peace, which is connected with HaShem, already teaches
196	us that it is not at the level of the world; it is above
197	the world. Two thousand years the Torah preceded
198	the world. And for the Torah to reach the world, the Jew needs
199	to bring the Torah down from the number three to the number
200	four. Why is the number four connected with the world? Because
201	the world was created in such a way that it has time and place,
202	and the reality of place is divided into four directions, four
203	winds
204	of heaven. The whole world is divided into four kinds. What
205	are the four kinds of
206	the world?
207	Inanimate, vegetable, animal,
208	and speaking. Also spiritually, and in Kabbalah, we
209	know that the world that HaShem created is divided into four
210	worlds: Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah,
211	and Asiyah. In the world there are also four elements: fire, wind,
212	water, and earth. This is connected to those same four levels. Yes,
213	the inanimate, which is earth, is the last, lowest
214	element, and above it is water, which is connected to the vegetable.
215	Water makes all kinds of things
216	grow in delight. And wind is the spirit of the living soul of
217	the animals, and fire belongs to the speaking. It is the highest
218	level of the speaking, which has the ability to connect
219	with the soul, which is also called flames of fire, like
220	a spiritual flame that HaShem implanted in the lower person so that
221	he could cleave to holiness
222	and to these. So if
223	so, the world is divided into four, but so that this world
224	not conceal and hide the reality of HaShem, as HaShem
225	created it to be so, not through its own fault, HaShem created
226	the world to be concealing
227	and hiding, HaShem gave the Jew in parallel the
228	Torah, for the Gimel is the power of the three, in order
229	to bring peace to the world. And how do we make peace, as
230	we said before? By revealing HaShem, blessed be He,
231	"He who makes peace in His heights, He will make peace
232	upon us," that is, the same peace made on high
233	between the camp of Michael, on the side of Chesed, and the camp of Gavriel, on the side of
234	Gevurah, is made upon us and upon all Israel when
235	we engage in Torah and bring peace
236	to the world. The whole Torah was given to make peace in the world.
